# Rally in price supported by weak dollar Copper prices pushed through the $8,

000/t ceiling in late **8400 3-M Price, LHS** September and have managed to stay well above this level in **8200 8000 US $ Effective** October, indicating positive sentiment for the red metal. **Exchange Rate, RHS (inverted)** Much of this bullishness is supported by a faster than **7800 7600** expected recovery in refined consumption (particularly in **7400** Asia) and the reduced concerns over growth and **7200** unemployment in Europe.  Growth is very uneven within the **7000** region and is likely to ease in the coming months due to **6800** possible upward pressure on the Euro.  It is reported that **6600** nations have agreed to avoid „competitive devaluation‟ of **6400** their currencies and push toward market-based exchange-rate **6200** systems during the G20 meetings.  Market participants are **6000Jan-10 Feb-10 Mar-10 Apr-10 May-10 Jun-10 Jul-10 Aug-10 Sep-10 Oct-10** paying more attention to US monetary policy, and are Data: LME, US Federal Reserve expecting another round of quantitative easing that may bring about lower interest rates, a weaker dollar, and therefore even higher copper prices in the coming months.  The dollar has depreciated by over 4% on a trade-weighted effective exchange rate basis between 23<sup>rd</sup> August and 22<sup>nd</sup> October.  Meanwhile copper prices have risen almost exactly in parallel with the movements in the dollar and this month the LME 3- month copper price has advanced from lows of $8,100/t on 1<sup>st</sup> October to a high of $8,520/t on 25<sup>th</sup> October.  Reduced estimates of the size of the second round of quantitative easing by the Fed led to the dollar strengthening earlier on this week leading to slightly lower copper prices at the time of writing of around $8,330/t. 

### Physical ETFs rushing into the market 

As the inflows of funds into commodities have continued to increase, it appears that the financial sector is convinced that there are still further gains to be made from copper.  Indeed, one of the popular topics of conversation during LME Week was talk about the potential impact on prices of physically backed ETPs (exchange-traded products) following the announcement from UK-based ETF Securities on 11<sup>th</sup> October that it was preparing to launch a range of physically backed industrial metal exchange traded commodities (ETCs).  According to an SEC filing, Blackrock is also LME price edges up while stocks seeking to launch a copper (exchange-traded fund) ETF, fall further in October initially backed by 121,000t of the metal.  This follows the LME cash price and stocks Jun 10 – Oct 10 **LME price ($/t)** SEC filing on 22<sup>nd</sup> October from JP Morgan for a similar **8500 LME Stocks** ETF, which would initially be backed by 61,800t of copper. **LME Cash Price** The company said that the shares are „designed to mirror as **8000** closely as possible the performance of the price of physical **7500** copper‟.  The combined volume from the two ETFs of 183,000t wo

uld represent 50% of the current LME stock **7000** level. Given the lack of clarity over the structure of these products it remains unclear as to how they will affect the **6500** market. LME price edges up while stocks

### SHFE stocks move in opposite direction to LME and Comex As prices have rallied over the last three months, stocks have seen an unbroken falling trend on both Comex and © 2010 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 16 Copper Monitor November 2010 www.crumonitor.com LME exchanges. LME stocks fell from 463,175t four months ago to 368,025t on 27th October, dropping by 5,775t in October alone. COMEX also saw stocks decline, down by more than 9,000t to 75,459t this month. The decline has mainly been driven by consumers‟ restocking activity, as demand has been better than expected and many consumers did not secure enough material on annual contracts so have had to dip into the spot market. However, demand from US wire and cable companies has remained soft over this past month and delivered premia are being quoted in a slightly lower range of 5-5.5¢/lb, compared to 5- 6.5¢/lb quoted a month ago. This softer demand tone is expected to carry forward into the next two months. As the holidays approach and the North American market should stay fairly quiet, with exchange stocks stabilising. Europe is in slightly better shape, with both wirerod and brass mills in the northern part of the region still fairly busy. Semis order activity in October was not as good as that in September but has certainly improved from the quiet summer. In addition, November is looking reasonably strong, especially in Germany. Consequently, spot premia are slightly higher than a month ago, now ranging within $90-105/t on a CIF Rotterdam basis. In Northern Europe, consumers have seen significant improvements in semis production volumes over the last three quarters, especially in the automotive and white goods sectors. In contrast, copper stocks on SHFE have been rising. In the Change in exchange stocks, 2010 last couple of weeks, stocks have risen by 18,828t to ‘000t 106,275t on 21st October, their highest level since the end of 26 August. Meanwhile, refined copper imports dropped i

n **LME Europe LME Asia** September by 9.5% to 241,771t before the national holiday **SHFE** at the beginning of October, according to the General 6 Administration of Customs.  Market participants expect that refined imports will continue to decrease in the coming -14 months due to the unfavourable arbitrage.  On 19th October, the Chinese Central Bank raised its benchmark one-year lending rate by 0.25 percentage points to 5.56% and the -34 deposit rate by the same amount to 2.5%.  This was the first increase in interest rates in almost three years, suggesting -54 that the government is keen to tackle its potential inflation H1 10 Q3 10 problems, particularly asset price bubbles.  The market has Data: LME, Comex, SFE* Quarter-to-date up to October 27<sup>th</sup> , 2010 absorbed this piece of news quickly and the SHFE price eased back from highs of RMB63,520/t on 15<sup>th</sup> October, last seen in July 2008.  Prices on SHFE have since recovered and are currently trading at around RMB63,700/t. 

We currently understand that there is very little buying interest in the market because of the high prices and consumers are starting to run down their inventories.  The spot premium for imported cathode in China has dropped to around $30-80/t in October, from $80-120/t a month ago.  Levels of $80/t were reported at the beginning of October while $30-40/t was quoted more recently as the SHFE price rose. Chinese traders report that very few deals are being concluded for cathode lately, since there is now more scrap available (probably as a result of the domestic car and home appliance scrappage and subsidy schemes that started more than a year ago).  In addition, many of the recent enquiries are mostly from speculators rather than consumers. 

### Annual premia for 2011 recovering 

As usual, contract terms were discussed during LME Week.  While no official announcements have been made we understand that Codelco has agreed a premium for its European customers of $98 for 2011 ($18 higher than the previous year).  We understand that the higher level reflects both higher freight rates and

expectations that demand in Europe will be higher than levels a year ago.  Meanwhile, expectations for the annual premium for China are very different amongst market participants.  While most agree that it will definitely be higher than $98/t given the demand outlook for the country, we have heard a range of levels suggested, varying between $100-120/t.  We have also heard reports of annual terms at $110/t for the Japanese, where refined consumption has been partly driven by semis exports to China.  Meanwhile, South Korea‟s Public Procurement Service said that it is considering term contracts for copper, joining the other buyers in the market. 

### Thoughts from LME Week - bullish across the market spectrum 

A rare scenario emerged this year in LME Week w

here everyone (miners, refiners, traders, banks etc) agreed to one consensus – bullish for the copper price over the next 12 months.  Analysts also agree that the refined market will move into a deficit in 2011, as production is not expected to keep pace with demand.  However, estimates of the deficit differed widely from 200,000t to 900,000t given the different opinions on consumption.  Taking China as an example, analysts outside the country were more optimistic on Chinese copper demand compared to those who are based in the country.  Despite these different perspectives, we still think that refined consumption in China will be robust in 2011.  We attribute this to a new wave of demand for renewable energy, stable power grid investment and higher personal income.  In its 12th five-year plan (proposals have now been submitted and will be finalised in March 2011), China is expected to focus on increasing domestic consumer demand by raising labours‟ incomes, narrowing the gap between the rich and the poor.  Discussions during the week also focused on the potential risks of higher prices on demand and the impact over the longer term.  Substitution and downsizing in downstream businesses is likely to accelerate, judging from product development trends during historical periods of high copper prices, with consumers forced to switch from copper to cheaper alternatives, such as aluminium in low voltage power cables and air conditioning tubes.  We estimate that net substitution losses in 2010 may amount to 300,000t, and will rise to 400,000t to 500,000t each year at current price levels.  Many believe that the producers are going to have more bargaining power in 2011 due to an expected shortage of copper, with market particpants expecting copper to trade between $9,000/t and $15,000/t during the coming year. 

### Resurgence of labour issues in Chile 

There have been no major production strikes at the mines so far this year but two labour contracts are due for renewal by the end of 2010; Codelco‟s Radomiro Tomić mine and Anglo American Plc and Xstrata Plc's Collahuasi unit (the 4th largest copper mine in the world), with combined mine production of around 800,000t of copper.  Radomiro Tomić‟s situation is complicated as Codelco has announced its intention to reduce the labour force across all its divisions and this has created discontent among the workforce. Miners at Collahuasi have turned down the company‟s latest offer (which included an $18,500 bonus) and have subsequently voted for strike action.  Both parties can now request arbitration which will delay a strike by five days.  The developments of these negotiations will set a benchmark for the 11 labour contracts due to be renewed next year and the likelihood of strike action in 2011 cannot be discounted. Q3 results of Escondida, Grasberg and Antamina all show a y-o-y decline in production volumes, mainly attributed to lower ore grades, which is a long term trend in the industry.

Data: CRU,WBMS||**_._**||||||**.**||||||**.**| © 2010 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 8 of 16 November 2010 Copper Monitor www.crumonitor.com # Consumption trends ## **Copper wirerod recovery drives consumption growth** Copper wirerod, the largest and most important semi-manufacture and the leading consumer of refined copper has been the main engine of the recovery in global consumption through 2010. We estimate that world consumption has risen 7.3% to 10.5Mt in the first nine months of 2010. Due to the exceptionally poor opening quarter of 2009, the first quarter of 2010 showed the strongest “apparent” performance with an impressive 10.7% year-on-year expansion. The encouraging momentum has continued through Q2 and Q3 with healthy year-on-year growth rates of 5.5% and 6.0% respectively. ## **A rare synchronised upturn has contributed to high and sustained growth** It is exceptionally rare to see a unified recovery in wirerod consumption across the four main regions of the world. It typically occurs only once in a decade - the last time was 2004 - which also very revealingly coincided with a strong surge in copper prices. Part of the reason for the concerted upturn is that the global financial crisis was so encompassing, with nearly every major region affected to a greater or lesser degree and for a shorter or longer duration. The world is also much more globalised than it was ten years ago, with the global supply chains of automobile components meaning that decisions to idle assembly lines in the US have a ripple effect on the supply chain all the way back to Asia, where many of the electrical components are sourced or assembled. The normalisation of manufacturing operations in the automotive, appliance and electronics industries, back to utilisation levels close to where they were operating before the onset of recession, has resulted in some necessary restocking. This is particularly so in these parts of the market where the business cycle is relatively short, expenditure

is relatively low and affordable, and to some degree discretionary, especially if it is incentivised by subsidies such as the hugely successful car scrappage schemes.  But the same cannot be said of the construction industry where the cycles are much deeper and prolonged and where the project expenditures are much greater and less discretionary.  These segments will inevitably take much more time to recover, especially in North America, Europe and Japan where the economic impact has been greatest and long lasting. 

## **Motor windings are the fastest recovering wire and cable segment** 

The rapid recovery in the early cycle automotive, home appliance and electronics industries is clearly benefitting the winding wire business which supplies electric motor manufacturers.  World consumption surged 16% year-on-year to 2.0Mt in Q1-Q3 2010, and there is every indication that growth will remain strong into Q4.  Copper winding wire demand is benefitting not only from an increase in the number of automobiles or appliances sold, but from the industry trend towards more hybrid vehicles which need additional motor windings for the electric engine (rising intensity of use).  Energy cables are the largest product segment in terms of volume and embrace everything from low voltage wires for automobiles and appliances, to building wire and general wiring, right up to high voltage power cables for industrial or utility customers.  Automotive wire, appliance wire and utility power cable demand is generally healthy globally, but building wire demand is only really improving in China, Brazil and India.  It remains generally depressed almost everywhere else for both residential housing and commercial property.  CRU

estimates that global market volumes have risen by 4.5% in Q1-Q3 2010 compared to the dismal state of business in 2009.  Copper communication cable demand is up 3.2% for the same period which again is more reflective of a modest gain from an artificially depressed base level in 2009. 

## **Steady upturn from a low base in North America and Europe** 

After the exceptionally weak Q4 2009, wirerod consumption in Europe and North American has risen steadily through 2010.  Growth prospects for the North American market in 2010 had been considered so remote that it was with surprise that limited gains from an extremely depressed base level have been realised.  CRU estimates that wirerod consumption has risen by 5% year-on-year in Q1-Q3 2010, with only Canada failing to achieve positive growth.  Western European prospects had seemed little better, and the emergence of the Greek financial crisis appeared to further undermine the potential for recovery. However, while it is the case that the UK, Ireland, Greece, Portugal and Spain remain among the weakest consuming markets in 2010, their combined tonnage is relatively low.  Much more important h

as been the faster recovery in the major markets of Germany, Italy and France which account for 60% of the tonnage consumed. There were brighter hopes for Eastern and Central Europe, mainly on the grounds that the catastrophic plunge in Russian cable production in 2009 could not be repeated. These expectations have been realised with a solid 24% year-on-year rise in copper cable production in Russia in H1 2010. ## **Stronger growth across Asia, although offtake in Q4 will decelerate** Asian markets, beginning with South Korea and China and later spreading to Taiwan, Japan and ASEAN, were the first to show signs of an upturn in Q1 and Q2 2009. Since then, it has been impressive how they have maintained the momentum of their recovery through 2010. South Korean copper wirerod consumption, which was barely affected by the recession in 2009, has risen by 6.1% in Q1-Q3 2010. Taiwan and Japan which saw their recoveries emerge later in 2009 have posted an even faster rate of growth compared to the weak prior year levels. Taiwanese consumption has increased by 10.5% so far this year while Japanese shipments have advanced 8.6%. There has also been a healthy improvement across ASEAN where we estimate that wirerod consumption has risen by 9.0% to date this year. But China continues to be the powerhouse of the improvement in the market this year. Consumption has climbed by 10.9% to 3.8Mt in the year to September and demand has exceeded 1.3Mt in each of the past two quarters, which marks a new record level. Chinese wirerod production is growing at an even faster pace than consumption as local Chinese mills expand their output to replace imports of wirerod from overseas. Moreover there is no deceleration in the pipeline of new Chinese copper wirerod projects (see _Industry News_ ) to boost local supply and production in the future at the expense of overseas exporters. Chinese wirerod importers reduced their tonnages in Q3 and production slowed in South Korea and Taiwan as a consequence. There is a more general expectation that consumption growth across Asia will moderate in Q4. Q4 2009 was the highest volume quarter for North East Asia so it is realistic to expect that the year-on-year rate of growth will decelerate. Moreover, the ending of the Japanese hybrid vehicle sales incentives scheme is already leading to an inventory adjustment process in the automotive components industry which will impact winding wire and wiring harness orders. # Industry News ## **Consumption** - The **International Trade Commission** issued a final affirmative vote in its antidumping investigation of US copper tube imports from China and Mexico. The **Department of Commerce** will publish its final antidumping orders in the **Federal Register** on 15th November 2010. Cash deposit rates for imports from Mexico will be: **IUSA** 24.89%, **Nacobre** 27.16% and all others 26.03%. The deposit for imports from China will amount to: **Golden Dragon** 11.25%, **Hailiang** 60.85%, **Zheijiang Naile** 36.05%, **Luvata** 36.05%, **Ningbo Jintian** 36.05% and all others 60.85%. - On 11th October UK-based **ETF Securities** announced that it intends to launch a range of physically backed industrial metal exchange traded commodities (ETCs), to include one for copper. **J.P.Morgan Chase & Co.** will also introduce a physical copper exchange-traded fund (ETF), according to a filing made on 22nd October to the **US Securities and Exchange Commission** . The © 2010 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 13 of 16 Copper Monitor November 2010 www.crumonitor.com - registered amount of shares is 6,180,000, which will include a maximum offering of US$80.87 per share. In addition, **BlackRock** plans to establish a similar product, the shares of which will each represent 10kg of copper. The proposed maximum aggregate offering price in the filing is US$999.9M. Based on 27th October‟s copper settlement price, that ETF alone would equate to a maximum of 121,000t of copper. ETFs are investment funds that trade like stocks on exchanges. With copper prices approaching all-time highs, investors are attracted by the increasingly bullish supply-demand fundamentals. Both funds would be backed by copper held in LME warehouses. **ScotiaMocatta** has spent almost two years trying to launch a similar product without success. - **Nexans** announced that it has agreed to make a proposal to **Draka Holding NV** , to negotiate an agreement for a recommended cash offer to purchase all of its outstanding ordinary shares at €15 per share, subject to certain conditions. - In late October, according to a **First Quantum Minerals** (FQM) spokesperson, reports that FQM lost an arbitration case in **the International Chamber of Commerce** (ICC) Court of Arbitration in Paris against the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) over its **Kolwezi tailings** project are "completely untrue". - In **Chile** , on Wednesday 13<sup>th</sup> October, the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) passed the modifications on the new **mining royalty bill** that the Chamber of Senates approved previously. The old mining royalty scheme considered a fixed rate of 4% on mines‟ operating income and a variable rate depending on their profitability.  The new

royalty came into effect immediately for new operations and from 2018 it will apply to all mines. Miners will pay 5% when their margins are less than or equal to 35%, and the rate will increase on a sliding scale up to 14% when operating margins are 85% or higher.  Mines already operating can voluntarily enter into a transitional rate of 4%-9% between 2010 and 2012 and get a new six-year stability contract for the 2018-2023 period.

Prior to production cutbacks in Q4 2008 in response to the sharp global economic downturn, Morenci was mining about 910,000t/d. ## **Exploration and Development** 



- **First Quantum Minerals** (FQM) announced on 18<sup>th</sup> October that it is purchasing 100% of the fully diluted shares of **Antares Minerals Inc.** Antares owns the **Haquira** copper-molybdenum-goldsilver project in southern Peru.  Haquira has sulphide ore resources (measured and indicated) of some 356Mt grading 0.63% Cu, 0.04g/t Au, 1.79g/t Ag and 0.014% Mo and oxide resources of some 215Mt grading 0.46% Cu.  A preliminary economic assessment of Haquira shows an initial investment of US$2.06B for a 20-year mine life.  Production is estimated at 230,000t/y for years 1-10 and 193,000t/y over the mine life.  FQM believe that a 2015 start-up date is feasible, however, further studies will be carried out.  Antares also owns the Cristo de Los Andes copper-gold project in Peru and has a 50% interest in the Rio Grande copper-gold project in Argentina.
